claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 8 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child in hospital for 15 weeks but claimant regularly spends on child
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

expected_eligibility.name: Alex
expected_eligibility.reason: Claimant lives in the UK; Child is 8 (under 16); Child lives with claimant; Child is not in local authority care; Child in hospital for 15 weeks but claimant regularly spends on child; Child is not fostered; Child does not work 24+ hours/week; Child has not started an apprenticeship in England; Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right
circumstances: Child is not in local authority care

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child.

**To begin, I need to know:** How old is the child (or children) you're claiming for?

Please tell me:
1. The child's name(s)
2. Their age(s)

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 8 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So I'm assessing eligibility for **Alex, who is 8 years old** and lives with you.

Since Alex is under 16, this is great news - children under 16 automatically qualify as "qualifying children" for Child Benefit purposes. However, there are still some other checks I need to go through to confirm your eligibility.

Let me continue with the next step:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question:** Since Alex is 8 years old, I need to confirm - is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not in any paid work at all?

(For an 8-year-old, this would typically be "yes" - they're not in full-time paid work - but I need to check this to proceed.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's only 8! He just goes to school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's what I expected - Alex is just in school, which is perfect. Let me continue with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question:** Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?

(Again, for an 8-year-old, this would typically be "yes" - children this young don't usually receive these benefits - but I need to confirm.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - he doesn't get any benefits in his own name. He's just a kid.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question:** Is Alex in any kind of apprenticeship?

(For an 8-year-old in school, the answer should be "no", but I need to confirm this.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - he's only 8! He's in primary school, not doing any apprenticeship.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's clear. Let me move forward:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Now I need to check your residency status.** There are several paths that can qualify you for Child Benefit. Let me ask some questions to determine which applies to you:

**First:** Do you normally live in the UK?

If not, I may need to check alternative residency pathways (such as EU Settlement Scheme status, being a Crown servant abroad, or other qualifying circumstances).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's perfect. Since you normally live in the UK, you meet the residency requirement. Let me proceed:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question:** Are you responsible for Alex? 

According to the rules, responsibility means either:
1. **Living with the child** - you mentioned Alex lives with you at home, so this should apply
2. OR contributing significantly to their upkeep (food, clothes, housing, pocket money, etc.)
3. OR paying maintenance under a court order or agreement

Since you mentioned Alex lives with you at home in Manchester, I believe this confirms you're responsible for him. Is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - Alex lives at home with me, so I'm responsible for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's confirmed. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Important question:** Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or could anyone else be making a claim for him?

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- A grandparent
- Another guardian or relative

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at any given time.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's clear. Let me proceed:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question:** Where is Alex currently living?

- Is he living at home with you normally?
- Or is he currently in hospital?
- In care (such as a children's home)?
- Being fostered?

You mentioned he lives with you at home, so I expect the answer is that he's living normally at home - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, Alex has been in hospital for a while now - about three and a half months. But I still regularly buy things for him - you know, his favorite snacks, magazines, clothes, that sort of thing.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that important information. That changes things - Alex is currently in hospital. Let me check the rules about children in hospital:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Important clarification about hospital stays:**

The rule is that Child Benefit can continue for up to 12 weeks cumulative (total) time in hospital or residential accommodation. There's also a linking rule: if Alex returns home within 28 days of leaving hospital, that time counts towards the 12-week limit.

**Key questions:**

1. You said Alex has been in hospital for about 3.5 months (roughly 15 weeks). Is this one continuous stay, or has he had multiple stays?
2. If multiple stays, what was the gap between them? (If less than 28 days, they count together towards the 12-week limit)
3. Has Alex ever been in hospital before this current stay?

This will help me determine if the cumulative time has exceeded the 12-week limit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been one continuous stay - he's been in the hospital ward for about 15 weeks straight now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I see - so it's one continuous stay of approximately 15 weeks, which exceeds the 12-week limit. Let me continue with the assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! Even though Alex has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks, there's an **important exception** to this rule.

**The question is:** Are you regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital?

You mentioned that you regularly buy things for him - his favorite snacks, magazines, clothes, and so on. This kind of regular spending is exactly what this rule refers to.

Can you confirm: **Yes, you are regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - I regularly spend money on him. I buy his clothes, magazines, and his favorite food while he's in there.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's an important exception. Because you're regularly spending money on Alex's upkeep while he's in hospital, you can continue to receive Child Benefit even though his hospital stay has exceeded 12 weeks. Let me proceed:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Final question:** Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's hospital accommodation or maintenance?

In other words:
- Is the local council paying for any part of his hospital care or accommodation? 
- Or are you responsible for any contributions?

Generally, you cannot get Child Benefit if the local council is fully funding the child's care.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying for anything - it's just the NHS hospital care. I'm not getting any payments from the council for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's the final piece. You've met all the eligibility requirements. Let me provide you with the outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **You ARE ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex**

### Summary of Your Situation:

**Child:** Alex (8 years old)  
**Current Status:** In hospital (approximately 15 weeks continuous stay)  
**Your Responsibility:** Living with Alex normally; regularly contributing to his care

### Why You're Eligible:

1. **Age:** Alex is 8 years old - well within the qualifying age for Child Benefit
2. **Not working full-time:** Alex is in primary school
3. **No disqualifying benefits:** Alex isn't receiving Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit
4. **Residency:** You live in the UK (Manchester)
5. **Responsibility:** You are responsible for Alex and he normally lives with you
6. **No other claimants:** Only you are claiming for Alex
7. **Hospital Exception:** Although Alex has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks, you qualify for an important exception because **you are regularly spending money on his upkeep** (clothes, magazines, food). This exception allows Child Benefit to continue beyond the 12-week limit.
8. **Council not paying:** The local council is not funding his care - only the NHS hospital care

### Next Steps:

- **Claim now** if you haven't already done so at: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit
- If you need to **report a change** to an existing claim, you can do so online
- Keep records of your regular spending on Alex while he's in hospital, as this supports your eligibility claim
- If Alex's circumstances change significantly, let HMRC know

I hope this is good news during what I imagine is a challenging time with Alex in hospital. If you have any other questions or need to claim for other children as well, please let me know!

reasonings: Alex is eligible for Child Benefit because: (1) He is 8 years old, which qualifies as a 'qualifying child' (under 16); (2) He is not working full-time; (3) He is not receiving benefits in his own right; (4) He is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship; (5) You normally live in the UK (Manchester), meeting residency requirements; (6) You are responsible for Alex as he lives with you; (7) No other person is claiming Child Benefit for Alex; (8) Although Alex has been in hospital for approximately 15 weeks (exceeding the standard 12-week limit), you are regularly spending money on his upkeep (clothes, magazines, food), which is an important exception to the 12-week rule; (9) The local council is not paying towards his accommodation or maintenance - only the NHS is providing hospital care.
arguments.overall_reasoning: You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. Although his hospital stay exceeds the usual 12-week continuous stay limit, the exception applies because you are regularly contributing to his maintenance and care by purchasing necessities for him. All other eligibility criteria are met: Alex qualifies as a child under the age limits, you live in the UK, you are responsible for him, and no other person is claiming for him. The local council is not funding his care."
